docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: Status as of 2026-10-23: Unreleased covers main up to the open-prefetch commit. Entries for features merged after 1.1.0 that were missing (2026-07-19 to 2026-08-13) were added under "Commands and flags".

docs.title: ANI
docs.text: • compute_ani reports af as containment scaled so skani's GTDB cut (AF >= 0.5) falls at containment 0.405, capped at 1. Before, af was the raw containment, which also carries identity (c ~ AF x identity^k), so ANI >= 95 and AF >= 0.5 behaved like ANI >= 96.75 and missed 6-12% of skani's GTDB pairs. Against skani on r232 families 49546, 4881357 and 216572, recall went from 0.918, 0.942 and 0.877 to 0.980, 0.984 and 0.970; precision went from 1.000 to 0.990, 0.997 and 0.993. ANI, c_ab and c_ba are unchanged. Fitted for k=21, c=125. Check: tests/skani_af.cpp.

docs.title: Open
docs.text: • ArchiveReader::open reads every CATL, ACCX, GIDX, QCOL and TAXN section with large preads before walking them. Before, they were faulted in a page at a time through the MADV_RANDOM mmap. On the r232 reps pack (12 parts) at dandycomp01fl, geodesic's pack open went from 20.5 s to 3.0 s cold. A single-genome genopack extract went from 12.9-27.4 s to 1.7-2.4 s (3 interleaved rounds each, identical FASTA). Check: tests/open_prefetch.cpp.

docs.title: Help text
docs.text:
• --help now matches the code for enrich --sketch-kmers (unset: single-k, k=16), build --thin (skips GSTX and GCOV only; taxon grouping stays on), repack (directory scan, then one sequential decompression pass) and reindex --sketch-syncmer (auto max(2, k/3), never inherited).
  • enrich description, --pcore and --markers now say what enrich builds: GSTX/GCOV (with --taxon-group and multi-k sketches), PCORE with --pcore, no CORE or GAMI; the marker panel drives marker completeness scoring.
  • reindex --skch: auto --sketch-syncmer is resolved after k is inherited from the existing SKCH, so an inherited k=21 gets s=7, not 5. Check: tests/reindex_syncmer_inherit.py.
  • build, enrich and reindex --sketch-kmers with one value now set k; before, the value was dropped (k stayed 16) while auto s was computed from it. Check: tests/sketch_kmers_single.py.
  • reindex no longer crashes on packs where every species has one genome (the GSTX step read element 0 of an empty list). Check: tests/reindex_singleton_species.py.

docs.title: dedup
docs.text:
• dedup confirms fingerprint + length candidates by an XXH3-128 hash of the decoded residues before tombstoning, so genomes that only share a sketch minimum are no longer removed.
  • Candidates are sorted by fingerprint then length; before, equal-fingerprint genomes of different lengths could separate true duplicates so they were never compared.
  • Genomes already in a TOMB section are skipped; before, a second run could keep an already-tombstoned genome and tombstone the live copy.
  • New --groups TSV (default dedup_groups.tsv) lists every candidate with its hash and action, also under --dry-run. Check: tests/dedup_sequence_confirm.py.

docs.title: Unified taxonomy: stable taxids
docs.text:
• taxonomy unify --stable-taxids-from <prior>/taxonomy.tsv (7887ad4): synthetic nodes whose full (rank, name) path exists in a prior unify's columnar taxonomy.tsv keep that taxid; new nodes are numbered above its maximum. Without it, export ids follow concept-hash order and a reunify after renaming 464,051 species reused 1,215,247 prior taxids for other taxa. Pass it on every reunify of a released taxonomy.
  • taxonomy unify --lineage-overrides <tsv> (834573a): replaces listed accessions' pack TAXN lineages at read time. Duplicate or absent accessions are errors.
  • Unify fails on shared taxids (365e976): export throws if two nodes would receive one stable or export taxid, instead of silently dropping the second.

docs.title: Quality
docs.text: • quality_score QCOL column (f88d727, merged ad3be6f): the continuous completeness-only score is stored in QCOL (axis support, unit Fraction01, U16, 0 = not scored), readable via ArchiveReader::qcol_reader().

docs.title: Commands and flags
docs.text:
• subset (490b34d): copy-only accession subset of an archive or multipart directory; no source FASTA or re-sketching.
  • extract --concat-contigs (a9e61cd) and --nmask (d1e0bd4): one N-joined record per genome, with a kaiku KNMASK01 side file.
  • neighbors (eb4228c): a priori nearest-in-DB member per query from derep .gpd clusters.
  • pcore bootstrap (7e6b310): archives without SEC_CORE build PCORE from --theta / --min-seg-aa / --frac-max-hash instead of being skipped.
  • taxonomy partition --contiguous / --cap (3bd0840): taxonomy-contiguous part filling with a per-group size cap.

docs.title: Unified taxonomy
docs.text:
• taxonomy unify <packs…>: reconciles the taxonomies of several independent .gpk packs into one taxdump (nodes/names/acc2taxid.dmp or columnar binary + TSV) without merging sequence data. Per-part TAXN reads run in parallel; output is deterministic.
  • NCBI reconciliation (--ncbi-taxdump, also on build and merge): taxa whose scientific name is unambiguous in the NCBI taxdump keep their native NCBI taxid (bit63=0); taxa NCBI does not name get a stable content-hash concept_id (bit63=1). The namespaces are disjoint, with no renumbering.
  • --preserve-taxids: accessions with an authoritative NCBI taxid (e.g. organelle host taxids) keep it verbatim, importing the taxid's real NCBI lineage down to a strain leaf. Stale ids remap via merged.dmp. On the RefSeq organelle set, accessions matching their authoritative host taxid rose from 98.3% to 99.997%.
  • --ncbi-backbone / --gtdb-replaces-prok: optionally folds the entire NCBI tree in as backbone nodes, excising NCBI's own Bacteria/Archaea descendants so GTDB stays authoritative for prokaryotes.
  • Performance: caches the NCBI taxdump parse in <dir>/.ncbi_taxdb.cache (parallel dmp parse, staleness-checked). A 2.1M-accession, 1.6M-node unify runs in ~40 s with the cache.
  • Fixes: accession lookup (find_accession) and scan_taxonomy skip tombstoned genomes, so in a multipart set extract reads the live copy in a later part instead of the deleted (empty) one, and taxonomy scans no longer list deleted accessions (src/archive.cpp).
  • Fixes: NcbiTaxdb name parsing dropped every name because a .dmp record terminator was left on the last field. Taxdump export flattened all taxids to 1..N; it now keeps native NCBI ids and renumbers only concept_ids above the maximum NCBI taxid.

docs.title: Quality tier: contamination decoupled
docs.text:
• quality_tier is completeness-only. The old NA-safe max over seven correlated contamination axes demoted 362,935 GTDB r232 genomes at 6.9% PPV against CheckM2; it is removed. LQ is now genuine incompleteness (comp_eff < 0.50) only. The single CheckM2-calibrated duplication channel D may cap HQ→MQ, and nothing forces LQ (src/check/run_check.cpp:181-197).
  • quality_score is completeness-only (compute_quality_score(comp_eff)), replacing the multiplicative completeness×contamination score.
  • GTDB r232 tiers: HQ 5,257,430 (55.16%), MQ 3,737,697 (39.22%), LQ 535,855 (5.62%); zero missing.

docs.title: Contamination: three reported channels
docs.text:
• contamination_channels reports D (duplication, the only CheckM2-calibrated axis), S (FracMinHash minority), and G (median of the correlated geometry axes). They are used for dereplication's D→S→G tiebreak, never as a discard gate.
  • New TSV columns: contam_D, contam_S, contam_G, contam_score (noisy-OR, display only), channels_fired, contamination_tnf_minor.

docs.title: Completeness: marker scoring for all genomes
docs.text:
• --markers scores marker completeness for every genome (score_all_completeness = scan_all || markers given), not only pass-A-flagged ones. Marker completeness populated for ~99% of GTDB r232 (was ~34%); validated against CheckM2 at slope 0.81, pooled bias ~0.
  • completeness_effective priority: marker → aamer_core → post_decontam, with cluster_relative admitted only as a soft corroborator.

docs.title: Pack write-safety
docs.text:
• check unions carried-forward QUAL records instead of overwriting them and refuses to drop build-time core_dup_mass. A subset rescore no longer deletes untouched genomes.
  • New --dup-restore flag re-injects the build-time duplication axis from a quality or cladesplit score TSV.
  • --scan-all forces every genome through pass-B (implied by --markers).

• Directory archive layout: .gpk is now a directory of section files plus toc.bin. Single-file .gpk archives are no longer produced; section binary structures (CATL, GIDX, ACCX, …) are unchanged. (Corrected 2026-10-23: current builders write a single .gpk file and ArchiveReader maps one file; see Format.)
  • Multipart sets via ArchiveSetReader: open a directory of part_*.gpk archives as one set. Per-accession routing across parts, aggregated stats, multipart-aware extract / fetch_by_accession / batch_fetch / fetch_sequence_slice / taxonomy_for_accession. LocatedGenomeMeta carries (part_index, part_path) so callers can disambiguate part-local genome_id values that may collide across parts.
  • SKCH V4 (seekable, dual-seed, multi-k): replaces V1/V2/V3 (now hard-rejected). 96-byte SkchSeekHdr, 16-byte SkchFrameDesc, 16 384 genomes per zstd-compressed frame, planar (n_real_bins / sigs1 / sigs2 / masks) with seeds default 42/43, up to 8 k-mer sizes (--sketch-kmers 16,21,31).
  • .gpd Geodesic Derep Archive Format v1 + DerepView reader: representatives, rep-only embedding matrix (default f16), accession_set_hash (xxh3-64 of sorted live accessions joined with \n), staleness levels (Valid / LayoutChangedSameLiveSet / StaleNewGenomes / StaleTombstones / Mismatch).
  • NTDB section: optional embedded NCBI nodes.dmp + names.dmp (zstd) for offline taxid resolution; built by coordinator --ntdb DIR. (Removed 2026-07-09 in be1b440; current archives have no NTDB section and coordinator has no --ntdb.)
  • inspect subcommand: reports SKCH layout (V3 vs V4 seekable, n_kmers, sketch_size, frame size, dual-seed presence) and preload memory cost. Accepts a single archive or a multipart directory.
  • taxonomy subcommand group: replaces the single genopack taxonomy invocation with show / normalize / partition / assign-taxids / diff / patch (the last accepts GTDB-Tk classify_summary directly via --gtdbtk).
  • coordinator --ntdb: NFS-coordinated distributed build can now embed an NTDB section in the merged archive. (Removed in be1b440.)
  • reindex extended: --force, --no-gidx, --txdb, --cidx FILE (+ --cidx-threads), --skch with full --sketch-kmer(s) / --sketch-size / --sketch-syncmer (+ --skch-threads). Use --skch --force to upgrade legacy SKCH layouts to V4 in place.
  • dedup is now in-place: tombstones duplicate genomes by content hash directly in the archive (--dry-run to preview); physical bytes reclaimed only by repack.
  • CLI surface trimmed: genopack similar and genopack cidx removed. The functionality remains in the C++ API (ArchiveReader::find_similar / find_similar_by_accession / find_contig_genome_id); HNSW is no longer built by default and is library-only. (Corrected 2026-10-23: ArchiveReader has no find_similar; only the HNSW section reader had one, and HNSW was removed in be1b440. Rank KMRX profiles with cosine_similarity.)
  • Default build flags: --taxon-group and --taxon-rank (genus) are on by default. build uses taxon-rank, while repack uses the separate --taxonomy-rank option.
  • stat --json and multipart support: stat accepts either a single archive directory or a multipart set; --json emits machine-readable output.
  • repack command: two-pass taxonomy-grouped reshard for fast per-taxon NFS access
  • Phase 1 reads only GenomeDirEntry arrays (~300 MB) instead of full blobs; builds complete routing table in minutes
  • Phase 2 sorts all genome records by (taxonomy, oph_fingerprint) in memory
  • Phase 3 single-pass decompress + route with OMP parallelism; cap eviction of the largest writer only minimises shard fragmentation
  • --taxonomy-rank g|f flag (genus default, family fallback)
  • -m / --max-memory flag to control eviction threshold
  • OpenMP parallel decompression in repack Phase 3
  • Fix: MmapFileReader::advise() page alignment: madvise() requires a page-aligned address. The raw data_ + offset pointer was not aligned, so every MADV_DONTNEED call on SKCH sections returned EINVAL. The address is now rounded down to the nearest 4 KiB page boundary, with the length extended accordingly. On large runs (e.g. GTDB r232, 5.2 M genomes), this caused sketch mmap pages to accumulate across waves and increased peak RSS by ~200-300 GiB.

• Initial release: single-file .gpk format
  • build, merge, stat, extract, slice, add, rm, taxonomy, taxdump, similar, cidx, reindex, dedup commands
  • SHRD / CATL / GIDX / ACCX / CIDX / TAXN / TXDB / KMRX / HNSW / TOMB sections
  • Columnar catalog with row-group predicate pushdown
  • HNSW approximate nearest-neighbour index on KMRX profiles
  • NCBI taxdump export (names.dmp / nodes.dmp / acc2taxid.dmp)
  • Columnar binary taxonomy export (acc2taxid.bin / taxnodes.bin)
  • Distributed build scripts
  • ScanEngine with I/O / worker thread separation (NFS and NVMe modes)
  • MEM-delta codec (k=31 seed + zstd verbatim residue)

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text: Status as of 2026-10-23: dedup describes the sequence-hash fix (2026-10-23); binaries built before it, including 2ac05b64, remove on fingerprint + length alone. Every subcommand and flag in genopack --help is documented here (checked by a per-command flag diff against the installed binary). The --help strings for enrich --sketch-kmers, build --thin, repack and reindex --sketch-syncmer were corrected to match the code on 2026-10-23; binaries built earlier, including 2ac05b64, still print the old text. The enrich description, enrich --pcore and enrich --markers were corrected the same day, and reindex --skch now resolves auto s after k is inherited. A single --sketch-kmers value now sets k in build, enrich and reindex, and reindex no longer crashes on packs where every species is a singleton (both fixed 2026-10-23; earlier binaries, including 2ac05b64, have both bugs).

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
genopack <command> [options]

All commands accept --help / -h for option details. Wherever a flag below takes an archive, the path may be either a single .gpk file or a directory containing one or more part_*.gpk (multipart set).

docs.title: build
docs.text:
Build a new archive from a TSV.

genopack build -i genomes.tsv -o mydb.gpk [options]

The output mydb.gpk is a single file (-o mydb also writes mydb.gpk). Defaults: per-taxon shard grouping (--taxon-group, genus rank), kmer-NN sort within shards, OPH sketches (--sketch, k=16, sketch size 10 000), auto codec. The CIDX contig index is opt-in (--cidx).

Flag Default Description -i / --input required unless --from-gpk Input TSV (accession\tfile_path\t[completeness\tcontamination\ttaxonomy\t…]); exactly one of -i and --from-gpk must be given -o / --output required Output archive file (.gpk; appended if missing) -t / --threads 16 I/O threads (decompression + compression) -z / --zstd-level 6 zstd compression level (1-22) -p / --parallel 1 Parallel build workers (auto-merge) --no-dict off Disable shared dictionary training --ref-dict off Use first genome in each shard as reference content dictionary --delta off Compress non-reference blobs against first genome via zstd prefix --mem-delta / --no-mem-delta on k=31 k-mer seeded exact-match encoding for highly similar shard groups --2bit / --no-2bit on Pack nucleotides to 2 bits/base before zstd (~1.5-2× extra compression) --cidx / --no-cidx off (skip) Build CIDX contig index (off by default; pass --cidx to build it) --kmer-sort / --no-kmer-sort on Sort genomes within each shard by kmer4 NN chain --taxon-group / --no-taxon-group on Group genomes into per-taxon shards (requires taxonomy column) --taxon-rank g Rank for grouping (g = genus, f = family) --sketch / --no-sketch on Compute OPH sketches --sketch-kmer 16 OPH sketch k-mer size --sketch-kmers 16,21,31 Comma list (e.g. 16,21,31) → multi-k SKCH in a single pass; one value (e.g. 21) gives a single-k SKCH at that k. Pass '' to use --sketch-kmer instead --sketch-size 10000 Number of OPH bins --sketch-syncmer -1 (auto: s=k/3) Open syncmer prefilter s (0 disables) --gstx / --no-gstx on Build GSTX genus-stats index (--no-gstx to disable) --pcore / --no-pcore on Build the dense PCORE per-genus small-contig reference (needed for small-contig contamination; dominant build cost and on-disk size). --no-pcore to disable --pcore-frac 100 FMH subsampling factor N for PCORE aamer extraction (keep 1/N aamers). Lower = denser; 1 = keep all. Overridden by GENOPACK_AAMER_FRAC or a --markers panel --tier off Emit a .ptier side-channel file for later genopack tier merge (records every (aamer_hash, genus_hash) pair for a global IDF tier table). Implies --pcore --micro-genus-threshold 0 (auto) Min genomes for a genus to get its own shard + GSTX/GCOV/FMHR consensus model; smaller genera are bin-packed and unmodeled. Auto: 4 (≤50k genomes), 8 (≤500k), 16 (≤2M), else 32 --markers auto Path to markers.mrk for build-time marker completeness scoring. Auto-resolved from $GENOPACK_DATA/markers.mrk or the install share dir --contam-panel auto Path to contamination .csp panel for build-time intra-genome duplication scoring. Auto-resolved from $GENOPACK_DATA/contamination.csp or the install share dir; absent → axis skipped --ncbi-taxdump unset Path to an NCBI taxdump dir (nodes.dmp+names.dmp). Lineage taxa whose scientific name is unambiguous in NCBI keep their native NCBI taxid; taxa NCBI doesn't have get a synthetic concept_id. See Unified Taxonomy --from-gpk unset Rebuild from an existing .gpk: stream decoded sequence from its shards instead of opening per-genome FASTA files. Mutually exclusive with -i --tmpdir /scratch or /tmp Directory for PCORE/SKCH spill files; use a fast local NVMe path --thin off Ingest-only preset: skips GSTX and GCOV, which enrich builds later; PCORE and GAMI still follow --pcore. --taxon-group is on by default and --thin does not turn it off; pass --no-taxon-group so shards flush by size, not genus --coordinator unset NFS manifest coordinator: manifest_dir:/output.gpk -v / --verbose off Verbose progress

docs.title: enrich
docs.text:
Rebuild a thin archive produced by build --thin into a new archive with GSTX and GCOV, reading sequences from the thin .gpk (no NFS opens). PCORE is added only with --pcore. Enrich never writes CORE or GAMI: the build path it uses returns before the GAMI step, and no build writes CORE. GSTX, and so GCOV, are accumulated only with taxon grouping and multi-k sketches (src/builder.cpp:1350), and both are off by default here, so pass --taxon-group and --sketch-kmers 16,21,31.

genopack enrich -i thin.gpk -o enriched.gpk [options]
Flag Default Description -i / --input required Thin source archive (.gpk) -o / --output required Output enriched archive (.gpk) -t / --threads 16 Worker threads --taxon-group off Group genomes by genus; required for GSTX and therefore GCOV --taxon-rank g Taxonomy rank for grouping (g = genus, f = family) --markers auto Marker panel (.mrk) for marker completeness scoring during the GCOV pass; if omitted, $GENOPACK_DATA/markers.mrk or the install share dir --contam-panel unset Contamination panel (.csp) for duplication scoring --sketch-kmers unset (single-k, k=16) Comma-separated k-mer sizes: several give a multi-k SKCH (e.g. 16,21,31), one value sets k --sketch-size 10000 OPH bins --sketch-syncmer auto Syncmer s (default: auto) --pcore off Also build PCORE. GAMI is not built; run genopack gami build afterwards --tmpdir /scratch or /tmp Directory for PCORE/SKCH spill files

docs.title: merge
docs.text:
Merge multiple .gpk archives into one. Uses parallel pwrite, with one thread per part.

genopack merge -l parts.txt -o merged.gpk
# or
genopack merge part1.gpk part2.gpk part3.gpk -o merged.gpk
Flag Default Description -l / --list Text file with one .gpk path per line -o / --output required Output path --ncbi-taxdump unset Reconcile the merged taxonomy against an NCBI taxdump dir: shared taxa keep native NCBI taxids --tmpdir $GENOPACK_SKETCH_SPILL_DIR, $GENOPACK_SPILL_DIR, /scratch, /tmp Directory for SKCH spill files during merge (no thread option) - No thread flag: merge copies each input part concurrently via std::async + pwrite (one task per part), so parallelism scales with the number of input archives

docs.title: stat
docs.text:
Print archive statistics.

genopack stat mydb.gpk [--json]

Output: generation, shard count, live/total genome count, total bp, compression ratio, per-section inventory. Accepts a single .gpk file or a multipart set; multipart sets show an aggregated total plus per-part breakdown.

docs.title: inspect
docs.text:
Report SKCH layout and preload memory cost.

genopack inspect mydb.gpk [--json]

For each archive (single or each part_*.gpk in a multipart directory) prints: live genome count, sketch_size (bins), mask_words (ceil(sketch_size/64)), the list of kmer_sizes stored, bytes per sketch per k, bytes per genome, and total preload size. Use this to decide whether to mmap-preload sketches or stream them frame-by-frame on memory-tight nodes. --json emits machine-readable output.

docs.title: neighbors
docs.text:
A priori nearest-in-DB member per query accession from the derep .gpd cluster structure (cluster rep = nearest representative-DB member, no alignment). For ancient-metasim absent-taxon placement.

genopack neighbors derep.gpd --accessions-file queries.txt -o neighbors.tsv
Flag Default Description derep required Derep .gpd file or directory of .gpd parts --accessions-file required Query accessions, one per line -o / --output stdout Output TSV

docs.title: extract
docs.text:
Extract genomes as FASTA.

genopack extract mydb.gpk [filters] -o out.fasta
Flag Description --accession ACC Extract genome(s) by accession (repeatable: --accession A --accession B) --accessions-file FILE Extract list of accessions (one per line) --min-completeness FLOAT Completeness filter (0-100) --max-contamination FLOAT Contamination filter -o / --out Output FASTA (default: stdout) --output-dir DIR Write one {accession}.fa per genome to this directory --concat-contigs One record per genome: contigs joined by N-runs, header = accession --concat-ns INT N-run length between contigs (default 300; must exceed the longest read) --nmask With --concat-contigs and -o: also write <out>.nmask (per-reference effective length + N-intervals, for kaiku) --manifest FILE Per-genome property TSV (bp, n_contigs, gc, completeness, contamination, oph_fingerprint, taxonomy) for the selected accessions, or the whole catalog when none are given. Metadata-only without -o; with -o it is written in the same pass as the FASTA

docs.title: slice
docs.text:
Extract a subsequence by accession and coordinates.

genopack slice mydb.gpk GCA_000008085.1 --start 100000 --length 5000 --fasta

The accession is a positional argument. --start (0-based) and --length are required; --fasta adds a FASTA header.

For archives without 2-bit packing, only the checkpoint blocks covering the region are decompressed. Archives built with the default build --2bit packing decompress the whole genome and then slice (src/shard.cpp, 2-bit branch of decompress_sequence_slice).

docs.title: add
docs.text:
Append genomes to an existing archive (new shard generation).

genopack add mydb.gpk -i new_genomes.tsv
Flag Default Description -i / --input required Input TSV of genomes to append

Existing shards are untouched. CATL, ACCX, GIDX, TAXN, TXDB, CIDX and KMRX each receive a new fragment. Use repack afterwards if taxonomy grouping is required.

docs.title: rm
docs.text:
Soft-delete (tombstone) genomes.

genopack rm mydb.gpk GCA_000001405 GCA_000002655

Records the genome ids in a new tombstone (TOMB) section. Physical space is not reclaimed; use repack to compact.

docs.title: dedup
docs.text:
Tombstone genomes whose sequence equals another genome's, keeping one copy.

genopack dedup mydb.gpk --dry-run --groups groups.tsv   # review first
genopack dedup mydb.gpk --groups removed.tsv
Flag Default Description --dry-run off Write the groups TSV and change nothing --groups dedup_groups.tsv Group-to-accession TSV, written on every run

Genomes already tombstoned are skipped. Candidates are genomes with equal OPH fingerprint and genome length. Each candidate's FASTA is decoded and hashed (XXH3-128 over residues only: header lines and line breaks are ignored, contig boundaries are kept). Only candidates with equal hashes are duplicates. In each duplicate set the genome with the highest completeness is kept (ties: lowest genome_id) and the rest are tombstoned in a new TOMB section; physical bytes are reclaimed only by repack. Residue case is hashed as stored, so a soft-masked copy is not a duplicate.

The groups TSV has one row per candidate genome: candidate_group, genome_id, accession, genome_length, oph_fingerprint, sequence_hash, completeness, action. action is keep, remove, or distinct (shares fingerprint and length but no other candidate has its sequence).

docs.title: subset
docs.text:
Subset an archive to a set of accessions by copying the kept genomes' sections (sequences, sketches, QUAL, taxonomy, KMRX) directly. This requires no source FASTA or re-sketching and preserves the original QUAL. For a multipart directory, subsets each part_*.gpk. Genome IDs are preserved (sparse); corpus-derived sections (GSTX/CIDX/HNSW) are dropped.

genopack subset input output --accessions-file accs.txt [options]
Flag Default Description input (required) Source .gpk archive or multipart directory output (required) Output .gpk (or directory, for a multipart source) --accessions-file (required) File of accessions to keep: one per line, or a TSV with an accession/name column -t, --threads 1 Threads for shard decompression

docs.title: repack
docs.text:
Re-shard an archive by taxonomy for fast per-taxon NFS access.

genopack repack input.gpk output.gpk [options]
Flag Default Description -t / --threads 1 OMP decompression threads -z / --zstd-level 6 Output compression level -m / --max-memory 32 Max buffered FASTA data in GB before eviction --taxonomy-rank g g = genus, f = family -v / --verbose off Log every source shard processed

When to use: After building a large archive with build --no-taxon-group, or after many add operations that scattered genomes across shards. A repacked archive allows geodesic-style tools to read only the ~1,900 shards belonging to Salmonella instead of all 24,000+ shards.

Algorithm: Three-phase two-pass design.

  1. Phase 1: Reads only GenomeDirEntry arrays from each shard (~300 MB total for a 3.1 TB archive). Builds a full genome→taxonomy routing table in memory.
  2. Phase 2: Sorts all genome records by (taxonomy, oph_fingerprint).
  3. Phase 3: Single sequential pass through the source archive; decompresses FASTAs with OMP parallelism; routes each genome to its pre-determined taxon writer; flushes the largest writer when memory cap is hit (minimises partial-shard fragmentation).

docs.title: taxonomy
docs.text: Group of taxonomy utilities. Each operation is its own subcommand.

docs.title: taxonomy show
docs.text:
genopack taxonomy show mydb.gpk [--accession ACC] [--json]

Print the lineage for one accession (or every accession when --accession is omitted). With --json, emits one JSON object per line.

docs.title: taxonomy normalize
docs.text:
genopack taxonomy normalize -i raw.tsv -o normalized.tsv [--ncbi-taxdump DIR]

Take an accession\ttaxonomy\tfile_path TSV and produce a normalized 10-rank lineage TSV (d,l,k,p,c,o,f,g,s,S). GTDB lineages are normalized by rank propagation. With --ncbi-taxdump, eukaryote and virus lineages are resolved against NCBI nodes.dmp + names.dmp; the dump is downloaded if absent or older than 30 days.

Accessions reused by different source files are resolved by decompressed-sequence content hash: exact repeats are dropped and distinct genomes get a ~dupN suffix.

Flag Default Description -i / --input required Input TSV (accession\ttaxonomy\tfile_path) -o / --output required Output normalized TSV --ncbi-taxdump unset NCBI taxdump dir for eukaryote/virus resolution --dup-manifest unset Write a TSV of resolved accession collisions (accession, file_path, resolved_accession, action, content_hash)

docs.title: taxonomy partition
docs.text:
genopack taxonomy partition -i normalized.tsv -n 8 -o parts/ [-r g]

Partition a normalized TSV into N balanced parts at a given rank (g = genus, f = family) for parallel/distributed builds, using LPT bin-packing. Every genome of one taxon lands in the same part, sorted by taxonomy. Writes part_0.tsv … part_{N-1}.tsv under the output directory.

Flag Default Description -i / --input required Normalized TSV (accession\ttaxonomy\tfile_path) -n / --parts required Number of output parts -o / --output-dir required Output directory -r / --rank g Partition rank: g = genus, f = family --contiguous off Fill parts in taxonomy order so sibling taxa land in the same part (lower read fan-out downstream) instead of size-only LPT. Use with --cap --cap 0 Max genomes per taxon group; larger groups are split into contiguous chunks of at most cap. 0 = no cap

docs.title: taxonomy assign-taxids
docs.text:
genopack taxonomy assign-taxids -i normalized.tsv -o registry.tsv [--acc-map acc2cid.tsv]

Assign canonical concept IDs (FNV-64(canonical_path) | (1<<63), deterministic, no central counter) to lineage paths and emit canonical_path\tconcept_id (sorted by path). Optionally writes a per-accession accession\tconcept_id\ttaxonomy map.

Flag Default Description -i / --input required Normalized TSV -o / --registry required Output registry TSV --acc-map unset Output per-accession TSV

docs.title: taxonomy diff
docs.text:
genopack taxonomy diff --current current.tsv --gtdb bac120_taxonomy.tsv --gtdb ar53_taxonomy.tsv -o out/

Diff a current genome set against a new GTDB release. Each genome is classified as unchanged, taxonomy_changed, needs_gtdbtk, dropped_from_gtdb or new_in_release; one TSV per category plus summary.txt go to -o / --output-dir. --current accepts the original input TSV or the genopack meta TSV. --gtdb is repeatable (pass bac120_taxonomy.tsv and ar53_taxonomy.tsv, or a merged file). With --write-unchanged, also writes the (often huge) unchanged.tsv.

docs.title: taxonomy patch
docs.text:
Patch taxonomy assignments in place, either against a .gpk archive or a flat input TSV.

# Patch the archive directly
genopack taxonomy patch --archive mydb.gpk --patch reassignments.tsv

# Patch an input TSV before rebuilding
genopack taxonomy patch --tsv genomes.tsv --patch reassignments.tsv [--tsv-out patched.tsv]

# GTDB-Tk classify_summary input
genopack taxonomy patch --archive mydb.gpk --patch gtdbtk.summary.tsv --gtdbtk

Default patch format is accession\tnew_taxonomy. --gtdbtk accepts GTDB-Tk's classify_summary format directly. --no-normalize disables 7→10 rank normalization (default: on).

docs.title: taxonomy unify
docs.text:
Reconcile the taxonomies of several independent .gpk packs into one common taxdump without merging their sequence data. The command reads each pack's lineage strings (TAXN), builds one tree, and writes nodes.dmp/names.dmp/acc2taxid.dmp (or columnar binary + TSV) covering every accession. The result provides one taxid space for per-pack mapping references and downstream classification. See Unified Taxonomy.

genopack taxonomy unify prok.gpk organelle.gpk viral.gpk \
    --ncbi-taxdump ./taxdump -o ./common_taxonomy [-f taxdump|columnar]
Flag Default Description inputs required Input .gpk packs (any number) -o / --output required Output directory -f / --format taxdump taxdump (NCBI nodes/names/acc2taxid.dmp) or columnar (binary + TSV) --ncbi-taxdump unset NCBI taxdump dir: taxa with an unambiguous NCBI name keep their native taxid; GTDB/other-only taxa get a synthetic concept_id --preserve-taxids unset TSV of accession → NCBI taxid (e.g. organelle host taxids). Those accessions keep the given taxid instead of resolving by name. Its NCBI lineage is imported down to a strain leaf. Stale ids remap via merged.dmp --ncbi-backbone off Fold the entire NCBI tree in as backbone nodes, so NCBI taxa without a reference genome still exist in the scaffold --gtdb-replaces-prok off With --ncbi-backbone: excise NCBI's Bacteria/Archaea descendants (anchors kept) so GTDB stays authoritative for prokaryotes --lineage-overrides unset accession\tlineage TSV replacing those accessions' TAXN lineages at read time (GTDB 7-rank lineages normalized as in taxonomy patch). Duplicate or absent accessions are errors --stable-taxids-from unset A prior unify's columnar taxonomy.tsv. Synthetic nodes whose full (rank, name) path exists there keep that taxid; new nodes are numbered above its maximum

Always pass --stable-taxids-from when reunifying a released taxonomy. Without it, synthetic ids are numbered in concept-hash order, so any added, removed or renamed node shifts later ids and old taxids can name other taxa. Unify fails if two nodes would share one taxid. See Unified Taxonomy.

Output is deterministic (identical inputs → identical output). The NCBI taxdump parse is cached to <taxdump-dir>/.ncbi_taxdb.cache.

docs.title: taxdump
docs.text:
Export taxonomy in NCBI or columnar binary format.

genopack taxdump mydb.gpk -f taxdump -o ./taxdump/
genopack taxdump mydb.gpk -f columnar -o ./taxonomy/
Flag Default Description -f / --format columnar taxdump or columnar -o / --output required Output directory Format Output files Description taxdump names.dmp, nodes.dmp, acc2taxid.dmp, empty merged.dmp and delnodes.dmp NCBI taxdump - Kraken/Kaiju compatible columnar acc2taxid.bin, taxnodes.bin, acc2taxid.tsv, taxonomy.tsv Fast offline lookup

docs.title: check
docs.text:
Compute per-genome quality scores (completeness, contamination) and write the QUAL section. See Quality Scoring for the underlying formulas.

genopack check mydb.gpk -o quality.tsv [options]
Flag Default Description pack required Path to .gpk archive or directory of parts -g / --genomes all in pack Optional accession list (one per line) -o / --output TSV output path for quality table -t / --threads 8 Threads --min-genus-size 3 Min genus members for saturated tier --leakage-threshold 0.05 Containment leakage threshold --recompute off Ignore existing QUAL section and force full rescan --scan-all off Force every genome through FASTA-level analysis (intrinsic completeness for all, rather than only flagged genomes); implied when --markers is given --markers unset Path to markers .mrk DB; enables marker-based completeness/redundancy scoring --cross-genus-margin 0.0 log-LR margin a foreign genus must beat the host by for cross_genus to flag a contig; 0 flags on any foreign LL > host LL --dup-restore unset Re-inject the build-time core_dup axis from a quality TSV or cladesplit score TSV, when a prior run overwrote QUAL without it

docs.title: ingest
docs.text:
Ingest external quality (CheckM2/anvi'o) into the archive as provenance-carrying XQAL columns.

genopack ingest mydb.gpk --checkm2 quality_report.tsv
Flag Default Description pack required Path to .gpk archive or directory of parts --checkm2 unset CheckM2 quality_report.tsv (Name/Completeness/Contamination) --anvio unset anvi'o completeness TSV (bin name/% completion/% redundancy)

docs.title: report
docs.text:
Emit a per-genome quality table resolved through a named profile. Each axis is sourced from one column (built-in rule or stored policy), and the report includes that column's provenance (tool/method). The selected fusion is recorded.

genopack report mydb.gpk -p best -o report.tsv
Flag Default Description pack required Path to .gpk archive or directory of parts -p / --profile best Profile name: built-in {intrinsic,external,calibrated,best} or a stored profile -o / --output stdout TSV output path --list off List built-in + stored profiles and the available provenance columns, then exit

docs.title: profile
docs.text: Manage named reporting/fusion profiles stored in the archive (SEC_PROF). Each operation is its own subcommand.

docs.title: profile add
docs.text:
genopack profile add mydb.gpk --name mypolicy -s completeness=checkm2:default -s contamination=intrinsic:default

Author a named profile pinning each axis to an exact column identity present in the archive.

Flag Default Description pack required Path to .gpk archive or directory of parts --name required Profile name (must not be a built-in name) --description unset Human-facing description (cosmetic; excluded from policy hash) -s / --select required Axis selector axis=tool:method[@cal][/tool:method[@cal]] (repeatable); the optional /… is a fallback

docs.title: profile list
docs.text:
genopack profile list mydb.gpk

List stored profiles and available columns.

docs.title: calibrate
docs.text:
Calibrate intrinsic completeness (aamer genus-core) against ground truth and write a CQAL section of calibrated per-genome columns. Ground truth: --checkm2 TSV, or the ingested XQAL if omitted. Also writes an isotonic+OLS JSON model and prints RMSE.

genopack calibrate mydb.gpk --checkm2 quality_report.tsv -o calibration.json
Flag Default Description archive required Path to .gpk archive or directory of parts --checkm2 unset CheckM2 TSV ground truth (falls back to ingested XQAL CheckM2 columns) -o / --output calibration.json Output JSON path for calibration model -t / --threads 8 Threads

docs.title: qcontig
docs.text:
Dump the per-contig quality overlay (SEC_QCONTIG): one row per (genome, contig) with offset/length/TNF/leakage, so you can see which contigs drive a genome's contamination.

genopack qcontig mydb.gpk --min-foreign 0.30 -o flagged_contigs.tsv
Flag Default Description pack required Path to .gpk archive or directory of parts -a / --accession all Restrict to one genome accession -o / --output stdout TSV output path --min-outlier 0.0 TNF channel (LONG contigs): emit contigs whose GCOV T² or SPE percentile ≥ this (e.g. 0.99) --min-foreign 0.0 Protein-aamer channel (SMALL contigs): emit contigs whose foreign_fraction ≥ this (e.g. 0.30) --min-lr 0.0 Protein-aamer channel: also require foreign log-LR ≥ this; pair with --min-foreign (e.g. 3.0) --min-leakage 0.0 Also flag contigs with containment-leakage score ≥ this

docs.title: decontaminate
docs.text:
Iteratively remove contaminated genomes (per-contig CCO above a threshold), rebuilding genus/family models from the survivors after each round.

genopack decontaminate mydb.gpk [--dry-run]
Flag Default Description archive required Path to .gpk archive --max-fmh-z 5.0 Remove genomes whose per-genus FMH-minority z (median+MAD delta from genus baseline) exceeds this; the genus-band signal --min-delta 0.02 Also require fmh_minority to exceed the genus baseline by this absolute amount (guards tight-baseline genera from z blow-up) --max-cco 1.5 Remove genomes whose CCO contamination % (per-contig T²∪SPE TNF-outlier bp vs the genus GCOV covariance) exceeds this; the distant-band signal (family/order/phylum). Needs contigs ≥20kb --max-iters 5 Max decontamination rounds -t / --threads 8 Threads --dry-run off Report what would be removed (with fmh_z/cco per axis) without modifying the archive

docs.title: gcov
docs.text:
Build (or rebuild) the GCOV (per-genus), FCOV (per-family) and FMHR (per-genus FracMinHash) sections in an existing .gpk archive; all three are rewritten together.

genopack gcov mydb.gpk
Flag Default Description archive required Path to .gpk archive -t / --threads 8 Parallel shard readers

docs.title: pcore
docs.text:
Build SEC_PCORE, the dense per-genus aamer reference containing every aamer and its prevalence. It detects foreign contigs of 1-2kb; the conserved-only CORE is too sparse at that length.

genopack pcore mydb.gpk
Flag Default Description archive required Path to .gpk archive or directory of parts -t / --threads 8 Parallel shard readers --members all live Reference accession list (one per line); only these genomes build the reference --theta 0.90 Conserved-core prevalence threshold; used only when the archive has no SEC_CORE --min-seg-aa 8 (= k) Min inter-stop AA segment length; used only when no SEC_CORE --frac-max-hash UINT64_MAX (dense) FracMinHash max hash; used only when no SEC_CORE

docs.title: gami
docs.text: SEC_GAMI tools: precomputed global aamer multiplicity index.

docs.title: gami build
docs.text:
genopack gami build mydb.gpk

Build and append SEC_GAMI v2 to a .gpk archive. Decodes PCORE/CORE once, serialises the global multiplicity index (exact sorted pairs, zstd), eliminating the 10-30 min GMI rebuild at each genopack check run.

Flag Default Description archive required Path to .gpk or directory of parts -t / --threads 8 Parallel decode threads

docs.title: tier
docs.text: IDF tier table tools: merge per-part .ptier files into a global .gtier, then stamp tier bytes into PCORE sections producing PCORE v2.

docs.title: tier merge
docs.text:
genopack tier merge -i part1.ptier -i part2.ptier -o global.gtier

Merge .ptier side-channel files from multi-part builds into a global .gtier IDF table.

Flag Default Description -i / --input required Input .ptier files (one per build part; repeatable) -o / --output required Output global .gtier table

docs.title: tier stamp
docs.text:
genopack tier stamp -i mydb.gpk --table global.gtier -o mydb.tier.gpk

Stamp per-aamer tier bytes from a global .gtier into a PCORE section, rewriting PCORE v1 → v2 in-place.

Flag Default Description -i / --input required Input .gpk archive --table required Global .gtier table from genopack tier merge -o / --output <input>.tier.gpk Output .gpk

docs.title: cladesplit
docs.text: Protein-aamer clade-split contamination tier (GUNC-style). Build a panel of genus-diagnostic aamers from reference genomes, then score genomes by lineage split.

docs.title: cladesplit build
docs.text:
genopack cladesplit build -i genomes.tsv -o panel.csp

Build a .csp panel from clean reference genomes.

Flag Default Description -i / --input required TSV (accession, file_path, taxonomy) -o / --output required Output .csp panel -t / --threads all cores Worker threads --frac-c 30 FracMinHash density 1/c on aamers --min-aa 8 Min inter-stop AA segment length --primitive aa Protein k-mer primitive: aamer | metamer | strobemer

docs.title: cladesplit score
docs.text:
genopack cladesplit score --gpk mydb.gpk --panel panel.csp -o scores.tsv

Score genomes against a .csp panel (per-genome minority_fraction).

Flag Default Description -i / --input TSV (accession, file_path), or use --gpk --gpk Score live genomes inside a .gpk archive directly (flag contamination in a genopack file) --panel required Panel .csp -o / --output required Output per-genome TSV (incl. redundancy_fraction) -t / --threads all cores Worker threads --frac-c 30 FracMinHash density 1/c (must match build) --min-aa 8 Min AA segment (must match build) --primitive aa Protein k-mer primitive (must match build): aamer | metamer | strobemer

docs.title: cladesplit aamers
docs.text:
genopack cladesplit aamers -i genomes.tsv -o dump.bin

Dump per-genome sorted-unique aamer sets (binary) for core/completeness R&D.

Flag Default Description -i / --input required TSV (accession, file_path) -o / --output required Output binary aamer dump -t / --threads all cores Worker threads --frac-c 30 FracMinHash density 1/c --min-aa 8 Min AA segment --primitive aa Protein k-mer primitive: aamer | metamer | strobemer

docs.title: markers
docs.text: Build or manage the SCG marker aamer panel (.mrk sidecar). Each operation is its own subcommand.

docs.title: markers build
docs.text:
genopack markers build --gtdbtk-db /path/to/gtdbtk_db -o markers.mrk

Build markers.mrk from GTDB-Tk MSA files (bac120 + ar53).

Flag Default Description --gtdbtk-db required GTDB-Tk reference database root -o / --output required Output .mrk file --threshold 0.30 Default presence threshold -t / --threads 1 Thread count --scale 1 FracMinHash scale factor: keep 1/N of hashes (ignored with --dayhoff6) --dayhoff6 off Build Dayhoff-6 k=12 syncmer profile pool (compact and less sensitive to divergence) --ic-threshold 0.25 Min per-column IC fraction to include k-mer positions (--dayhoff6 only) --expected-min-frac 0.50 A marker is counted as expected for a genus only if detectable (≥1 IC-passing syncmer) in at least this fraction of the genus's reference genomes; mirrors CheckM2's single-copy universality criterion

docs.title: markers remerge
docs.text:
genopack markers remerge markers.mrk

Append the pre-merged pool to an existing .mrk panel (in place) so MarkerReader uses its zero-copy mmap path instead of copying ~450MB per worker. This does not require source genomes.

Flag Default Description panel required Path to .mrk panel

docs.title: markers score
docs.text:
genopack markers score --fasta genome.fna --markers markers.mrk --genus g__Escherichia

Score a FASTA file for SCG marker completeness.

Flag Default Description --fasta required Input FASTA file --markers required Markers .mrk file --genus required Target genus key (e.g. g__Escherichia) --min-hits 1 Floor on hits per marker; the effective call threshold is max(--min-hits, query_kmers / 20)

docs.title: bench-grid
docs.text:
Heterogeneous spike-fraction × ANI-distance benchmark from a manifest TSV.

genopack bench-grid mydb.gpk --manifest manifest.tsv -o results.tsv

docs.title: Similarity search and contig lookup (library-only)
docs.text:
There is no genopack similar or genopack cidx CLI. KMRX profiles and CIDX contig→genome lookup are exposed through the C++ API only:

  • ArchiveReader::kmer_profile(...) / kmer_profile_by_accession(...) plus cosine_similarity(a, b): there is no built-in top-k search.
  • ArchiveReader::find_contig_genome_id(accession): CIDX binary search, ~150M queries/s/core.

See API → Similarity & contig lookup.

docs.title: reindex
docs.text:
Build or rebuild auxiliary index sections in place.

genopack reindex mydb.gpk [options]
Flag Default Description --force off Rebuild indexes even if already present --no-gidx off Skip GIDX (useful when only --skch is needed and GIDX is absent/unwanted) --no-gstx off Skip the GSTX genus-stats index --no-qual off Skip the QUAL per-genome quality build --gcov off Rebuild GCOV/FCOV/FMHR (full shard rescan). When GSTX and GCOV both exist afterwards, reindex clears the stale-stats header flag that merge sets --txdb off Build the taxonomy tree (TXDB) from existing TAXN lineage strings --cidx FILE unset Build the contig accession index (CIDX) from a build TSV (accession\ttaxonomy\tfile_path) --cidx-threads 8 Threads for parallel FASTA decompression while indexing contigs --skch off Re-sketch every genome into one coalesced SKCH section; pre-existing SKCH sections are dropped --skch-threads 8 Threads for parallel sketch computation --sketch-kmer inherit / 16 OPH k-mer size for a single-k SKCH section --sketch-kmers unset (single-k) Comma list (e.g. 16,21,31) → multi-k SKCH v2; one value sets k. Takes precedence over --sketch-kmer --sketch-size inherit / 10000 OPH sketch size --sketch-syncmer -1 (auto) Open-syncmer prefilter s (0 disables). Auto is max(2, k/3) with k the smallest --sketch-kmers value, else the resolved single k (--sketch-kmer, else the existing SKCH's k, else 16). s itself is never inherited from existing SKCH sections (only k and size are)

Typical uses: an archive built with build --no-cidx later wants contig lookup (--cidx genomes.tsv); a TAXN-only archive needs the tree (--txdb); SKCH layout needs to be upgraded to V4 seekable (--skch --force); or a multi-k variant is needed (--skch --sketch-kmers 16,21,31 --force).

docs.title: verify
docs.text:
genopack verify mydb.gpk [--strict] [--coverage-only] [--verbose]

Runs two checks. Semantic coverage cross-checks per-genome and per-genus section row counts against the catalog from the TOC only, without a data scan. SKCH (per k, every k must cover the whole catalog), QUAL, GIDX, ACCX, and CATL rows must equal the genome count. GSTX and other compute sections are reported as presence + coverage, not gated. Byte-level checksums cover TailLocator, TocHeader, and per-section XXH128 content. The command exits 0 if all checks pass and non-zero on any failure.

Flag Default Description archive required Archive directory to verify --strict off Fail if any section lacks a content checksum --coverage-only off Run only the section-coverage cross-check; skip byte-level checksums (seconds) --verbose off Print OK lines in addition to failures

docs.title: coordinator
docs.text:
NFS-coordinated assembly mode for distributed builds. Workers run build --coordinator <manifest_dir>:<output.gpk>; the coordinator process waits for the expected number of worker manifests, then merges parts into a single archive.

genopack coordinator -o mydb.gpk --workers 64 --nfs-dir /shared/manifests/
Flag Default Description -o / --output required Final merged archive path --workers required Expected number of worker manifests --nfs-dir required Shared directory where workers drop manifests

docs.title: Binary Format
docs.text:
Status as of 2026-10-23: checked against include/genopack/format.hpp (GPK3, FORMAT_MAJOR 3, FORMAT_MINOR 0). TailLocator is 128 bytes; the section table lists every SEC_* constant; the MetaBundle fast-open directory is documented below. The open sequence now includes the metadata prefetch (step 5).

A .gpk archive is a single file: FileHeader, then appended sections, a MetaBundle directory, the TOC and a 128-byte TailLocator at end of file. Sections can be appended without rewriting existing data; the TOC is rewritten with each generation and the TailLocator points to the current one. Multipart sets (used for very large or distributed builds) are directories containing one or more part_*.gpk files. ArchiveSetReader opens them as one archive. build -o mydb writes mydb.gpk.

On-disk form. Builders write one .gpk file (src/builder.cpp, since 440fea5) and ArchiveReader memory-maps that file. The 1.0.0 changelog described a directory of section files plus toc.bin; current code does not produce that layout.

docs.text: FileHeadermagic · version · UUID · created_ts · flags · endian_abi_tag · build_params_hash · generation · shard-set identity · dir back-anchor 256 B SHRD × Ncompressed genome shards; each generation appended, old shards untouched variable CATLcolumnar genome metadata (SoA, sorted by oph_fingerprint) GIDXgenome_id → (section_id, dir_index, catl_row) ACCXFNV-1a hash table: accession → genome_id CIDXsorted (FNV-1a-64(contig), genome_id) array TAXNFNV-1a hash table: accession → lineage string TXDBfull taxonomy tree (taxid/parent/rank/name + acc→taxid) SKCHOPH (one-permutation hash) sketches: V4 seekable, dual-seed, multi-k KMRXoptional float[n × 136] L2-normalised k=4 tetranucleotide profiles (library-only) TOMBtombstone records for soft-deleted genomes TOCSectionDesc[] (raw, uncompressed), one record per section TailLocatorfixed footer at EOF, points to TOC offset and MetaBundle 128 B

dual-seed; multi-k) KMRX K-mer profiles Library-only. float[n × 136] L2-normalised k=4 tetranucleotide frequencies TOMB Tombstone Soft-deleted genome_id records TOCB TOC block TocHeader + SectionDesc[] directory BPRM Build parameters Self-describing build parameters, one per archive; its params_hash is mirrored in FileHeader.build_params_hash GSTX Genus sketch stats Per-genus consensus sketch, p90 distance and TNF centroid GCOV Genus covariance Per-genus biological covariance (whitening basis + calibrated quantiles) FCOV Family covariance Same layout as GCOV, keyed by family hash FMHR FracMinHash reference Per-genus FracMinHash reference sketches (k=21, c=125) CORE Prevalence cores Per-genus conserved aamer cores (content-hashed models) PCOR Dense aamer reference SEC_PCORE: every aamer per genus with u8 prevalence; docs.title: FileHeader: 256 bytes
docs.text:
Offsets 0..39 are byte-identical to the older GPK2 header (magic/version/uuid/created_at/flags). The former GPK2 reserved[88] region now holds named GPK3 fields followed by a smaller reserved tail. A static_assert(sizeof(FileHeader) == 256) enforces the size.

Offset Size Field Description 0 4 B magic GPK3 (0x334B5047) 4 2 B version_major Breaking format change (FORMAT_MAJOR = 3) 6 2 B version_minor Backward-compatible extension (current: 0) 8 8 B file_uuid_lo Archive UUID low 64 bits (stable across generations) 16 8 B file_uuid_hi Archive UUID high 64 bits 24 8 B created_at_unix Unix timestamp of initial build 32 8 B flags Header flags; bit 0 = FH_FLAG_STATS_STALE (derived genus/quality sections dropped by merge) 40 8 B endian_abi_tag == ENDIAN_ABI_TAG byte-order / ABI canary 48 8 B build_params_hash BPRM params_hash (cross-section param link) 56 8 B generation Durable generation, bumped on each seal 64 8 B shard_set_uuid_lo Shard-set identity low 64 bits 72 8 B shard_set_uuid_hi Shard-set identity high 64 bits 80 4 B shard_id Durable shard id, assigned at first seal 84 4 B _pad0 88 8 B dir_back_offset Header-side anchor → directory (torn-tail recovery) 96 8 B dir_back_size Directory byte size 104 16 B dir_back_xxh128 Directory content hash 120 8 B dir_back_generation Front/back agreement check 128 128 B reserved Zero-padded to 256

Note: generation is present in both FileHeader (offset 56, durable) and TocHeader.

docs.title: Shard section (SHRD)
docs.text:
SHRD variable ShardHeadermagic · shard_id · n_genomes · codec · dict_sizedir_offset · dict_offset · blob_area_offset · checkpoint_offset 128 B GenomeDirEntry[n_genomes]genome_id · oph_fingerprint · blob_offset · blob_len_cmp · blob_len_rawcheckpoint_idx · n_checkpoints; sorted by oph_fingerprint 64 B × n zstd dictionaryoptional; ZSTD_DICT and REF_DICT codecs only dict_size B Blob areablob[0] · blob[1] · ...; each independently decompressible variable CheckpointEntry[]optional; symbol_offset · block_offset · enables sub-genome slice 16 B × n

Genomes are sorted by oph_fingerprint within each shard. Nearby OPH values indicate similar k-mer content, maximising zstd LDM reuse and shared dictionary effectiveness.
